concerns.text: T104 requires the convergence monitor to flag iterations with 'tolerance < 1e-4', but the log schema T101 writes ('iteration_id, sample_size, converged, max_iterations, error_message') has no tolerance field. The monitor's verification ('report reflects the actual convergence log entries') is unexecutable against the artifact T101 produces — either T101 must add a tolerance field or T104 must drop that criterion.

T103 asserts split_half_results.json 'contains a binary replication status', but T102 defines that file's schema as per-sample-size aggregated rates ('replication_rate', 'iterations'), not per-iteration binary outcomes. The T103 verification condition cannot be checked against the artifact T102 actually produces; specify which field constitutes the 'binary replication status' or point T103 at the per-iteration records.

All V01–V09 items are rendered as unchecked boxes '- [ ]' despite the header stating they are 'verified complete' and 'do not redo'. An implementer or agent parsing checkbox state will redo preserved work. Mark them '- [x]' or restructure as a non-checklist table.

T105 is too coarse for a single task: it bundles full-domain execution across 5 paradigms × 2 grids × 2 kernels × 5 effect sizes × 3 alphas × 3 tolerances, plus logistic models, sensitivity metrics, timing capture, and success-criteria validation. Split into per-stage execution tasks (e.g., per-paradigm run, aggregation, validation) so each has a discrete verifiable deliverable; the atomizer will otherwise have to guess the boundaries.

T102 says per-iteration records 'must also satisfy' replication_result.schema.yaml 'fields where applicable' — 'where applicable' is ambiguous for an implementer deciding which of the 12 required fields (e.g., pipeline_config_hash, target_effect_size, magnitude_tolerance_pct) must be populated. Enumerate the required fields or state that all schema-required fields apply.

T103's verification requires 're-running the command from clean derived outputs reproduces the CSV and JSON' but does not define 'clean derived outputs' (which directories to delete, whether raw data is retained). Specify the reset procedure (e.g., 'rm -rf data/derived/ data/aggregated/ and re-run') so the reproducibility check is deterministic.
